messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis  
Details: The test `testBoundaryRangeTooLarge` shows that when the CMAESOptimizer is given very wide bounds (close to Double.MAX_VALUE), it ends up calling the fitness function with NaN parameters. The test uses bounds defined by `-tooLarge` and `tooLarge` where `tooLarge` is `FastMath.nextUp(Double.MAX_VALUE / 2)`. The bug report also suspects the encoding and decoding of parameters inside the optimizer with these extreme bounds result in NaN due to overflow or improper normalization.

The constructor of `CMAESOptimizer` simply configures the optimizer instance but does not enforce bounds validation or processing at construction time. The key behavior to diagnose is likely inside `CMAESOptimizer.optimize(...)` or related helper methods that encode/decode parameters with respect to lower and upper bounds.

Since the test fails with NaN parameters passed to the fitness function, this indicates an overflow or numeric instability in translating parameters to the normalized space or back. The optimizer's internal encode/decode scheme likely uses the bound range difference (upper - lower) for normalization which for these extreme values would overflow beyond the maximum double precision value, resulting in NaN during calculations. This results in the fitness function receiving NaN input and subsequently throwing an exception, failing the test.

The root cause likely stems from a missing validation or check that the difference between upper and lower bounds does not exceed a certain magnitude (less than Double.MAX_VALUE) before proceeding with normalization inside CMAESOptimizer or its parent classes. This aligns with the bug report which suggested the issue is inside `FitnessFunction.encode/decode`.

Thus, the bug happened because the optimizer does not guard against extremely wide bounds causing overflow in normalization, resulting in NaN parameter values passed to the fitness function.

Next, it would be helpful to inspect the relevant encode/decode methods in CMAESOptimizer or its superclass which handle parameter normalization with respect to bounds. This will confirm the exact overflow and normalization logic causing NaN propagation.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
